result.summary:
Re-gated the incremental amendment commit 30919e94 (on top of already-security-reviewed 4efff094) against `git diff main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/definitions/promotion.ex lib/letflow/routers/promotions.ex`. Scope test: applies -- this touches an apply_review/4 mutation gate (lookup-by-ID + response-shaping) on a tenant-scoped entity. Assessed all 8 invariants against the diff:

INV-1 (tenant data isolation) -- APPLIES, PASS. The diff adds no new query. `verify_rehearsed/2`'s only data access is the pre-existing, already-reviewed `Letflow.Definitions.get_latest_assertion_run/2` (lib/letflow/definitions.ex:1179-1197), unchanged by this commit -- confirmed it calls `Repo.one(query, prefix: prefix)` with `prefix = Keyword.fetch!(opts, :prefix)`, i.e. (a) satisfied (prefix-scoped), (b)/(c) not implicated (no new table/migration, no new tenant_id field). The amendment is pure in-memory branching on the struct already fetched.
INV-2 -- NOT-APPLICABLE (S4 not started).
INV-3 -- NOT-APPLICABLE (S5 not started).
INV-4 (secrets) -- APPLIES, PASS. No secret material touched; the two new atoms/messages carry no credential or token data.
INV-5 -- NOT-APPLICABLE (S4 not started; this is a status-gate on an existing authorized review lookup, not a new lookup-by-ID surface).
INV-6 (new data-access path proves scoping) -- APPLIES, PASS. This handoff itself is the proof; INV-1 above states which sub-checks applied and how confirmed.
INV-7 (no SQL interpolation) -- APPLIES, PASS. No `Repo.query`/raw SQL anywhere in the diff; `verify_rehearsed/2` only pattern-matches/branches on an already-fetched struct field (`assertion_run.status`).
INV-8 (no unhandled crashes) -- APPLIES, PASS. The new branch is a plain `if/else` on a field of a struct already confirmed non-nil by the preceding `case` (`{:ok, assertion_run}`); no new bare pattern match that can raise on realistic input.

Race closure (task's second acceptance criterion): confirmed by reading the full `with` chain in `apply_review/4` (`with {:ok, review} <- get_review, :ok <- verify_apply_digest, :ok <- verify_approved, :ok <- verify_rehearsed(review, plan_digest, opts) do do_apply_review(...) end`) -- `verify_rehearsed/2` now checks `assertion_run.status not in [:running]` strictly before the `assertions_failed == 0` check (both inside the same digest-match branch), so a `:running` row (whose `assertions_failed` is always 0 by construction) can no longer fall through to the previously-exploitable `:ok` branch. Any `{:error, :assertion_run_in_progress}` short-circuits the `with` and `do_apply_review/3` (and therefore `promote_definition/3`) is never reached -- there is no other call site of `do_apply_review/3` in the module. This matches the new regression test in the same commit (`test/letflow/routers/req077_promotion_pipeline_test.exs`, 'rejects an in-progress rehearsal') which asserts the review stays `:approved` and the target definition is untouched on a `:running` fixture, and the sibling `:teardown_failed` test proves the fix is additive (excludes only `:running`, not narrowed to `:passed`-only). No remaining bypass found.

Information disclosure (task's third acceptance criterion): the new 409 for `:assertion_run_in_progress` ('the most recent assertion run for this review has not finished yet; wait for it to complete or re-run assertions before applying') discloses nothing beyond what the caller -- an authenticated actor on this review's own tenant, already authorized to call apply on this review_id -- already necessarily knows (that a rehearsal was attempted). It is the same information class as the three existing 409s for this review_id (`:assertion_run_missing`, `:assertion_run_digest_mismatch`, `:assertion_run_failed`): no cross-tenant data, no digest value, no other tenant's review state. `lib/letflow/routers/promotions.ex` clause ordering confirmed: the new `render_apply(conn, {:error, :assertion_run_in_progress})` clause (lib/letflow/routers/promotions.ex:646) sits among distinct-atom sibling clauses with no catch-all above it that could shadow it, and produces `Response.conflict/2` (409) via the same helper as its siblings -- consistent shape, no new status-code class introduced.

Verdict: PASS. The amendment closes the OQ-2 gap completely, introduces no new invariant violation, and stays within the disclosure envelope of the already-reviewed base.
